name: Siemens FS140
amazon: Siemens FS140 FirstSurge Pro whole house surge protector
description: Siemens' 140 kA Type 2 whole-house surge protector with a NEMA 4X enclosure, audible alarm and ground monitoring, for homes with heavy lightning exposure.
quick: Type 2, 140 kA, NEMA 4X Indoor/Outdoor Enclosure. Siemens' 140 kA Type 2 whole-house surge protector with a NEMA 4X enclosure, audible alarm and ground monitoring, for homes with heavy lightning exposure.
bestFor: Homes in lightning-prone areas that want maximum capacity
skipIf: Your panel has no room for a large external housing
specs: External, any brand panel up to 400A; NEMA 4X indoor/outdoor
Green LEDs, red service light, audible alarm, ground monitoring
verdict: The FS140 is the whole-house surge protector to ask your electrician for if you want maximum capacity and a device that tells you loudly when it has worn out.

**140 kA of headroom.** Siemens rates the FirstSurge Pro at 140,000 amps of surge capacity. No single surge comes close to that; the point is service life. Each surge wears the MOVs a little, and a bigger rating means more years before replacement in lightning-prone areas. It is a [Type 2 device](/glossary/surge-protective-device/), so it goes on the load side of the main breaker, wired to a double-pole breaker (Siemens recommends 20A) in any brand of panel up to 400A.

**Low let-through voltage.** The UL 1449 voltage protection ratings are 600V line-to-neutral, line-to-ground and neutral-to-ground, and 900V line-to-line. Lower is better, and these are strong numbers for a residential device. Keep the leads short and straight, since long leads raise the real let-through.

**It tells you when it fails.** Three-stage notification uses green LEDs, a red service light and an audible alarm. Ground reference monitoring also flags a bad neutral-to-ground bond. The NEMA 4X enclosure is rated for indoor or outdoor mounting. Siemens lists a 10-year product and connected equipment warranty.

Electricians like its capacity and loud alarm; the main complaint is the bulky housing on cramped panels. Siemens is phasing the FS140 out in favor of the [Siemens FSPD140](/gear/siemens-fspd140/). It is the top pick in our [best whole house surge protector](/best-whole-house-surge-protector/) guide; the [Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA](/gear/eaton-chsptultra/) is the value alternative.

600V VPR on L-N, L-G and N-G modes
Audible alarm plus LED service indication
Ground reference monitoring flags bonding faults
NEMA 4X enclosure for indoor or outdoor mounting
cons: Type 2 only, so it cannot go ahead of the main breaker
Being phased out for the FSPD140
Bulky housing on crowded panels

faqs.q: Is the Siemens FS140 a Type 1 or Type 2 surge protector?
faqs.a: Type 2. Siemens lists the FirstSurge FS140 as a UL 1449 Type 2 device for use downstream of the service disconnect. That means it mounts at the panel on a double-pole breaker, not ahead of the main breaker at the meter. For line-side installs, look at a Type 1 device such as the Square D HEPD80.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Siemens FS140 and FSPD140?
faqs.a: Both are 140 kA Type 2 devices in NEMA 4X enclosures with audible alarms. The newer BoltShield FSPD140 replaces the FS140 and adds a Form C dry contact, phase-loss monitoring and EMI filtering. Its VPR is 700V L-N versus 600V on the FS140, so the older unit has slightly lower let-through on paper.

name: Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA
amazon: Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA whole house surge protector
description: Eaton's 108 kA Type 2 whole-house surge protector in a NEMA 4 housing that mounts on any brand of panel, a common electrician favorite for value.
quick: Type 2, 108 kA, Panel Mounted. Eaton's 108 kA Type 2 whole-house surge protector in a NEMA 4 housing that mounts on any brand of panel, a common electrician favorite for value.
bestFor: Most homes that want high capacity without paying for premium
skipIf: You want an audible alarm when protection fails
specs: External, any brand load center; NEMA 4
Limited lifetime with connected equipment coverage
verdict: The CHSPT2ULTRA gives you most of the capacity of the premium devices for noticeably less, which is why so many electricians install it by default.

**108 kA per phase.** Eaton rates it at 108 kA peak surge current per phase and 20 kA nominal discharge current (In). That In figure matters: it is the surge level the device must survive 15 times in UL 1449 testing, and 20 kA is the highest In rating UL assigns. It is a [Type 2 surge protective device](/glossary/surge-protective-device/), connected on the load side of the main breaker.

**Let-through numbers.** The voltage protection ratings are 600V line-to-neutral, 600V line-to-ground, 800V neutral-to-ground and 1000V line-to-line. The N-G and L-L figures are a step behind the [Siemens FS140](/gear/siemens-fs140/), but the line-to-neutral rating, which covers most household loads, is the same 600V.

**Fits any panel.** The NEMA 4 housing attaches to the outside of any manufacturer's load center through a knockout, and Eaton also offers load centers with a built-in mounting spot for it. LEDs show the status of each protection mode. Eaton's literature lists a limited lifetime warranty with connected equipment coverage; read the terms, as claims depend on proper installation and grounding.

Owners and electricians praise the price-to-capacity ratio. The common complaint is small, dim status LEDs that are easy to ignore, and there is no audible alarm. It is the value pick in our [best whole house surge protector](/best-whole-house-surge-protector/) guide. Compare it with the [Square D HEPD80](/gear/square-d-hepd80/) if you need a Type 1 rating.

20 kA nominal discharge rating
600V VPR line-to-neutral and line-to-ground

cons: Type 2 only, load side of the main breaker

faqs.q: Does the Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA work with non-Eaton panels?
faqs.a: Yes. Eaton says it can be attached to the outside of any manufacturer's load center. Your electrician mounts the NEMA 4 housing through a panel knockout and wires it to a double-pole breaker. It is a Type 2 device, so it must go on the load side of the main breaker.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA and the Siemens FS140?
faqs.a: Both are Type 2 devices that mount on any panel. The Siemens is rated at 140 kA and adds an audible alarm and ground monitoring, with VPRs of 600V on L-N, L-G and N-G. The Eaton is rated at 108 kA per phase with an 800V N-G rating, LEDs only, and usually costs less.

name: Square D HEPD80
amazon: Square D HEPD80 whole house surge protector
description: A compact 80 kA Type 1 surge protector from Square D with a NEMA 4X housing that fits any brand of panel and can go on the line side of the main breaker.
quick: Type 1, Compact 80 kA Unit, Knockout or Surface Install. A compact 80 kA Type 1 surge protector from Square D with a NEMA 4X housing that fits any brand of panel and can go on the line side of the main breaker.
bestFor: Tight panels or line-side installs that need a Type 1 device
skipIf: You live in a lightning-heavy area on long overhead lines
specs: Type 1, compact 80 kA unit, knockout or surface install
Knockout or surface mount, any brand; NEMA 4X
verdict: The HEPD80 is the compact, flexible choice: a Type 1 device small enough for a tight panel, with protection ratings that match larger units.

**Type 1 means more install options.** Schneider Electric lists the HEPD80 as a UL 1449 Type 1 [surge protective device](/glossary/surge-protective-device/). Type 1 units can be installed on the line side of the main breaker as well as the load side, which helps when a meter-main combo or outdoor disconnect leaves no good spot on the load side. It is rated for 120/240V single-phase panels of any brand.

**80 kA is enough for most homes.** Square D rates it at 80 kA per phase, with a 10 kA nominal discharge rating and a 25 kA short-circuit rating. That is less headroom than the 140 kA [Siemens FS140](/gear/siemens-fs140/), so in lightning-heavy regions on long overhead lines it may need replacing sooner. In a typical suburban home it is plenty.

**Small but well rated.** The housing measures about 3.2 x 3.7 x 2.1 inches with a NEMA 4X non-metallic rating, and the leads are 34 inches long, so it can sit right next to the breaker. The voltage protection ratings are 600V line-to-neutral and line-to-ground, 900V neutral-to-ground and 1000V line-to-line. Square D lists a 5-year limited warranty.

Electricians like its size and Type 1 listing. The main complaint is a single small green LED that is hard to see, so mount it where you will check it. It is the smallest-footprint pick in our [best whole house surge protector](/best-whole-house-surge-protector/) guide; the [Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA](/gear/eaton-chsptultra/) offers more capacity at the panel.

faqs.q: Can the Square D HEPD80 be installed before the main breaker?
faqs.a: Yes, if local code and your utility allow it. Schneider Electric lists the HEPD80 as a UL 1449 Type 1 device, which can be installed on the line side of the main breaker as well as the load side. Line-side work must be done by a licensed electrician and may need utility approval.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Square D HEPD80 and the Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA?
faqs.a: The HEPD80 is a compact Type 1 device rated at 80 kA per phase with a 10 kA nominal discharge rating. The Eaton is a larger Type 2 device rated at 108 kA per phase with a 20 kA nominal rating. Both list 600V line-to-neutral VPR. Choose the Square D for a tight or line-side install.

name: Intermatic IG2240-IMSK
amazon: Intermatic IG2240-IMSK whole house surge protector
description: Intermatic's Type 1 or 2 surge protector with three user-replaceable iModules in an indoor metal housing, for homeowners who want to swap worn modules, not the whole unit.
quick: Type 1 or 2, 50 kA, Replaceable iModules. Intermatic's Type 1 or 2 surge protector with three user-replaceable iModules in an indoor metal housing, for homeowners who want to swap worn modules, not the whole unit.
bestFor: Homeowners who want to replace worn modules themselves
skipIf: You need an outdoor-rated enclosure at the meter
specs: Type 1 or 2, replaceable iModules, indoor metal box
Blue power and green protection LEDs on each iModule
verdict: The IG2240-IMSK stands out for one feature: when its protection wears out, you replace a plug-in module instead of calling an electrician to replace the whole device.

**Replaceable iModules.** Intermatic's SmartGuard design uses three iModules with blue power and green protection LEDs. When a module's green light goes out, you flip the built-in module power switch and slide in a new one. The tamper-proof doors only open when a module is being inserted. That is the reason to choose it over a sealed unit.

**Ratings.** It is listed for Type 1 or Type 2 installation on 120/240V single-phase service, with six modes of protection and TPMOV thermally protected varistors. Intermatic rates it at 50 kA per phase, with 10 kA nominal discharge and 10 kA short-circuit ratings. The voltage protection ratings are 800V line-to-neutral, 700V neutral-to-ground, and 1500V line-to-ground and line-to-line. Those are higher than the 600V figures on the [Siemens FS140](/gear/siemens-fs140/), so let-through is less tight. See the [surge protective device](/glossary/surge-protective-device/) glossary for what VPR means.

**Indoor metal box.** The IMSK version uses an indoor Type 1 metal enclosure with 32-inch leads, so it belongs next to an indoor panel, not outside at the meter. Intermatic lists a 10-year base warranty, 3 years on modules, and a 10-year connected equipment warranty.

Owners like the module swap and clear status lights. The main complaint is the higher VPRs. It appears in our [best whole house surge protector](/best-whole-house-surge-protector/) guide; for lower let-through at a similar price, look at the [Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA](/gear/eaton-chsptultra/).

Type 1 or Type 2 listing

faqs.q: Can I replace the modules on the Intermatic IG2240-IMSK myself?
faqs.a: Yes, that is the design. The IG2240-IMSK holds three iModules with status LEDs. When a module's green protection light goes out, you switch off the built-in module power switch, remove the old module and insert a new one. The base unit stays wired in place, so no electrician is needed for a module swap.

faqs.q: Is the Intermatic IG2240-IMSK rated for outdoor installation?
faqs.a: No. The IMSK version uses an indoor Type 1 metal enclosure, so it belongs next to an indoor panel. The device itself is listed for Type 1 or Type 2 applications, but an outdoor meter or disconnect location needs a weather-rated enclosure, such as the NEMA 4X Siemens FS140.

name: Leviton 51120-1
description: A 50 kA Type 2 panel protector from Leviton in a steel NEMA 1 housing, a widely stocked choice for typical homes with modest lightning exposure.
quick: Type 2, 50 kA, 120/240 V Split Phase, Panel Mount. A 50 kA Type 2 panel protector from Leviton in a steel NEMA 1 housing, a widely stocked choice for typical homes with modest lightning exposure.
bestFor: Typical suburban homes with modest lightning exposure
skipIf: You want the lowest let-through voltage or an audible alarm
specs: Limited lifetime with connected equipment coverage
verdict: The 51120-1 is a sound, widely stocked panel protector for an ordinary suburban home, though its ratings trail the newer devices in this category.

**The ratings.** Leviton lists it as a UL 1449 Type 2 [surge protective device](/glossary/surge-protective-device/) for 120/240V single-phase panels, with 4-mode protection and a 50 kA maximum surge current per mode. The nominal discharge rating is 3 kA and the short-circuit rating is 10 kA. Leviton recommends a 20A double-pole breaker.

**Let-through is higher.** The voltage protection ratings are 800V line-to-neutral and 1200V line-to-line. Compare that with 600V line-to-neutral on the [Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA](/gear/eaton-chsptultra/) and [Siemens FS140](/gear/siemens-fs140/). A lower VPR means less of a surge reaches your electronics, so this unit is better suited to areas with modest lightning activity and underground service.

**Steel box, simple status.** The enclosure is powder-coated steel, NEMA 1, for indoor mounting next to the panel. Protection status LEDs show each mode; there is no audible alarm or dry contact. Leviton lists a limited lifetime warranty with connected equipment coverage. Leviton has marked the 51120-1 as discontinued and lists replacement models, so check stock before you plan around it.

Electricians like its build and the Leviton name. The main complaints are the higher VPRs and modest capacity. It is the known-brand pick in our [best whole house surge protector](/best-whole-house-surge-protector/) guide; the [Square D HEPD80](/gear/square-d-hepd80/) is a compact alternative with lower let-through.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Leviton 51120-1 and the Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA?
faqs.a: Both are Type 2 devices for 120/240V panels. The Eaton is rated at 108 kA per phase with a 20 kA nominal discharge rating and 600V line-to-neutral VPR. The Leviton is rated at 50 kA per mode, 3 kA nominal, and 800V line-to-neutral. The Eaton offers more capacity and lower let-through.

name: GE THQLSURGE
description: A breaker-style surge protector that plugs into two spaces in GE THQL panels, the fastest install for compatible GE load centers with room to spare.
quick: Plug-In Breaker Format for GE Panels. A breaker-style surge protector that plugs into two spaces in GE THQL panels, the fastest install for compatible GE load centers with room to spare.
bestFor: GE THQL panels with two free breaker spaces
skipIf: Your panel is not a compatible GE load center
specs: Plugs into 2 spaces in GE THQL-compatible panels
50 kA per phase, 25 kA per mode
Plug-in breaker format for GE panels
verdict: The THQLSURGE is the easiest way to add whole-house surge protection to a compatible GE panel, as long as you accept lower capacity than external devices.

**It installs like a breaker.** The THQLSURGE has the shape of a double-pole breaker and plugs into two spaces in GE THQL-compatible load centers. A pigtail lands on the neutral bar. There is no knockout and no external box, and the connection to the bus is as short as it gets, which helps keep let-through voltage down. ABB, which now owns GE's electrical line, lists it as a Type 1 [surge protective device](/glossary/surge-protective-device/) for service entrance or subpanel locations.

**Lower capacity.** A GE/ABB product sheet lists 50 kA per phase and 25 kA per mode, with a 10 kA nominal discharge rating. That is well below the 108-140 kA of the [Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA](/gear/eaton-chsptultra/) or [Siemens FS140](/gear/siemens-fs140/), so it wears out sooner in areas with frequent lightning.

**Check before you buy.** It only fits compatible GE panels with two free adjacent spaces. Status indication is a small indicator on the breaker face, so check it after storms. GE has discontinued the original THQLSURGE; the current version is the THQLSURGE2, which ABB rates at 25 kA per phase. Square D sells similar breaker-style devices for its QO and Homeline panels.

Electricians like how fast it goes in. The main complaints are the lower capacity and limited status display. It is the easiest-install pick in our [best whole house surge protector](/best-whole-house-surge-protector/) guide.

faqs.q: Will the GE THQLSURGE fit my panel?
faqs.a: Only if you have a GE load center that accepts THQL plug-in breakers and two free adjacent spaces. It plugs onto the bus like a double-pole breaker and needs a pigtail to the neutral bar. Other brands, such as Square D QO and Homeline, need their own breaker-style surge devices.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the GE THQLSURGE and THQLSURGE2?
faqs.a: The THQLSURGE2 is the current replacement for the discontinued THQLSURGE. Both plug into GE THQL panels. ABB lists the THQLSURGE2 at 25 kA per phase as a Type 1 device, while a GE sheet lists the original at 50 kA per phase. Check the exact rating on the package before buying.

name: Siemens BoltShield FSPD140
amazon: Siemens BoltShield FSPD140 whole house surge protector
description: Siemens' 140 kA Type 2 BoltShield surge protector, the FS140's replacement, adding a dry contact, phase-loss monitoring and EMI filtering in a NEMA 4X housing.
quick: Type 2, 140 kA, Dry Contact and Audible Alarm. Siemens' 140 kA Type 2 BoltShield surge protector, the FS140's replacement, adding a dry contact, phase-loss monitoring and EMI filtering in a NEMA 4X housing.
bestFor: Smart homes that want alarm contacts and maximum capacity
skipIf: You want the lowest possible VPR on a budget
specs: Type 2, 140 kA, dry contact, EMI filtering
3 green LEDs, red GRM LED, audible alarm, Form C dry contact
verdict: The FSPD140 is Siemens' current 140 kA whole-house device and the replacement for the FS140, with better monitoring and filtering in exchange for slightly higher let-through ratings.

**Same capacity, newer standard.** Siemens rates the BoltShield FSPD140 at 140 kA, with a 20 kA nominal discharge rating and a 200 kA short-circuit rating. It is a UL 1449 5th Edition Type 2 [surge protective device](/glossary/surge-protective-device/), so it mounts on the load side of the main breaker, protecting all modes: line-to-neutral, line-to-ground and neutral-to-ground.

**Monitoring is the upgrade.** Three green LEDs show each line, a red LED flashes for a ground reference fault (neutral-to-ground voltage above 20V), and an audible alarm sounds on failure. It adds phase-loss monitoring and a Form C dry contact rated 240V 2A, which can feed a home automation input or alarm panel. It also includes UL 1283 EMI/RFI filtering.

**VPR trade-off.** The voltage protection ratings are 700V on line-to-neutral, line-to-ground and neutral-to-ground, and 1200V line-to-line, with a 180V MCOV. The older [Siemens FS140](/gear/siemens-fs140/) lists 600V and 900V. The FSPD140's higher MCOV gives more margin against normal voltage swings, at the cost of slightly higher let-through. The NEMA 4X polycarbonate housing measures about 7.95 x 3.06 x 2.75 inches and supports flush, flange or through-hole mounting.

Its strengths are the dry contact and detailed status lights; the drawback is a larger housing than compact units on tight panels. Compare the field in our [best whole house surge protector](/best-whole-house-surge-protector/) guide; the [Eaton CHSPT2ULTRA](/gear/eaton-chsptultra/) is the value option.

faqs.q: Does the Siemens FSPD140 replace the FS140?
faqs.a: Yes. Retailers note the FirstSurge FS140 is being phased out and replaced by the BoltShield FSPD140. Both are 140 kA Type 2 devices in NEMA 4X housings. The FSPD140 adds a Form C dry contact, phase-loss monitoring and EMI filtering, and is listed to the newer UL 1449 5th Edition.

faqs.q: What does the dry contact on the Siemens FSPD140 do?
faqs.a: It lets the surge protector report its status to another system. The Form C contact, rated 240V 2A, changes state when the device detects a fault. An electrician can wire it to an alarm panel or a smart home input, so you get a notification instead of relying on someone to see the LEDs.
